reviews.comment: MEEN 613 - Engineering Dynamics, you know what this is. Don't B.S., and you'll come out ok. This course covers a LOT of ground, but it's worth it IF you put the work in. Professor Kim does a great job at explaining the topics. You WILL need to study you a** off. That said, coordinate transformations and 3D Rigid Body Dynamics is useful.
MEEN 659 Sound and Vibration Measurements covers the 1-D, 2-D, and 3-D Wave Equation in depth using complex algebra. Absolutely worth it! Dr. Kim teaches well, AND you obvi
Better than other 363 profs.
Good professor. Tries to make sure people actually learn what he is teaching and helped me out.

Prof does not post solutions to any homework's over semester, only post answers. Incredibly hard to learn, test are nothing like homework or review test. Entire grade is essentially test grades, test are graded extremely tough. Lecture slides often skip steps on how to actually solve example problems.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst 363 prof.

The lectures are extremely hard to follow. He will essentially talk through a bunch of concepts and if you have a question, you will get a mediocre at best reply. Looking around the class on a normal day, almost everyone can be seen doing something else with their time. Class test averages were always failing. One good thing is he curved BIG!

Dr. Kim may seem boring but the course itself can give anyone a tough reputation. My friends were taking professors such as Delgado and Balawi; Kim's HW and test problems are designed in a much more digestible fashion than others. Study his method of solving problems and the test and HWs are very doable. Much easier compared to other profs. for 363
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid him. Let me fit as much as I can: The homeworks/projects have nothing to do with the test material, he comes off as rude/unhelpful when asked a question in class, he has no idea what he is talking about in office hours on the project covering the whole semester, he never responds to emails, he grades the hardest, his slides are unfollowable.

I've had bad professors, but Dr. Kim takes the crown. Terrible at lecturing and just sits there and plays with code that he can't even get to work, rude to students when they ask questions in class, grades extremely hard, gives exams way harder than other profs for same class. Easily the most ignorant professor that I have ever had.
Avoid Dr. Kim at all cost. Seems like a great guy but this class needs some major changing. Exams were very long and the average for both the midterm and final were around 65. AVOID.

Seems like a great guy. This class is in need of some major overhaul. Youre forced to go to lectures but you can probably skip them and learn better on your own . The HW you can try your best on it but it wont matter for the exams. His practice exams are useless. Not enough in class examples to even know whats going on. Typical MEEN things :)

Hard to understand what we are expected to do/know in this class. HW is purely programming while exams are all hand written computations. You don't really learn much from the lectures (since he just types the code given on the slides) . Much of the material is presented in pure mathematical jargon without any example as to how to solve the problems

Dr. Kim was a wonderful teacher to have for this class, however the class was extremely difficult (my advisor told me students struggle with 363 a lot). I approached Dr. Kim as I was worried for my grade, but he was reassuring and extremely helpful. I would definitely take this class with him. If you struggle, I suggest talking to Dr. Kim for help.

Definitely cares about students learning, an adept coder. However, I had to learn most of the material from the textbook. Provides codes for you to use in your homework assignments, but even so, don't procrastinate. If you get stuck on a coding assignment, get help as fast as you can.

The class is a joke. Homework has nothing to do with lecture. The exam has nothing to do with homework or lecture. Gets difficult at end. Kim will not regrade anything even if the TA made an obvious mistake. Applied a nice curve to midterm and final.

Dr. Kim is one of the most difficult profs I have had. The code he provides for the homework has tons of errors, and his exams are much harder than any other professors. He makes mistakes in lectures because he is unprepared, and when there is a grading issue he refuses to give points back. He makes it very clear he is there for research.

Dr. Kim makes mistakes nonstop in lectures and expects you to figure out the hw even though hes not teaching correctly. Struggles to be clear due to language barrier. Exams aren't like hw. Sums up A&M engineering professors in general.

Great professor who teaches the material well. The class is pretty complicated but Dr. Kim is your best shot at doing well in it. Do the homework and the practice exam and you will be ready for his test. Each exam had a curve that put the average close to an 80 so he pretty generous with the exam grades.
Dr Kim is awesome. Make sure you attend his lectures. Also, attend recitations as well; yes it is time consuming but you understand the content better.

Dr. Kim teaching Vibrations. His lectures do aid well in learning key concepts. The hard part of the class was I'd say the hw. Theres a total of 8 assignments (not online) with coding. If you want to stay ahead of the curve, put a lot of work on the hw's and go to class (drops hw grades if you do). Exams are non-common non-cumulative. Nice curve!!
Dr. Kim didn't like regrading exams if they were wrongly marked and his final exam was nothing like the final exam practice problems. Overall he's a difficult person.

Dr. Kim's class becomes easy if you pay attention and keep up with the lecture notes. There are not many homework assignments, but they do a good job of keeping you up to speed on the course material. The exam problems are consistent with covered course material. One of the best professors I have had so far.

Kim does not speak english well and will assume that you have every bit of base knowledge from prerequisite courses. He rushes through material, and will not repeat himself for the sake of his students. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you won't get two homework grades (out of the 6 all semester) dropped if you miss more than once. Trash.

Dr. Kim is very difficult to work with if you have disability services. He will take attendance when he knows you'll be missing to take the exam at a different scheduled time and puts off signing forms and replying to emails. He also has long lectures where he skips a lot of steps. His exams are harder for some sections than others.
Attendance wasn't mandatory, but it helped with extra credit. Yong-Joe Kim is the best dynamics teacher at TAMU.

Professor Kim's lectures were pretty boring to be honest, but he's a great guy. The material wasn't too difficult to understand if you paid some attention and did the homework. The exams are a lot like the homework, but the final blindsided a lot of people this semester. Do the homework and study them for exams and really study for the final.
